mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies anticipate lower revenues.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a surge in supply-side activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to stronger economic growth prospects.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months signals accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real interest rates remain low.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between low CPIAUCSL and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) declines for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth prospects dim.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS declines for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over three consecutive months signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as broader economic activity picks up.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is growing at a rate of more than 2% year-over-year and real GDP (GDPC1) is expanding, it signals robust supply-side growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations improve.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO YoY growth > 2% and GDPC1 expanding
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of INDPRO and GDPC1 on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
